questionBank.title: Object-Oriented Programming — Week 4 Question Bank
questionBank.subject: Object-Oriented Programming
questionBank.syllabusCoverage: Concept of Constructor; types of Constructors (default, parameterized and copy); Encapsulation and Information Hiding; public and private access specifiers; this and new keywords.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of a constructor in C++?

options.B: To initialize an object when it is created

questions.question: Which statement about a C++ constructor is correct?

options.A: It must have a return type
options.B: It has the same name as its class and no return type
options.D: It can only be called manually

questions.question: A constructor that can be called without arguments is commonly called a:

options.B: Parameterized constructor

questions.question: Which constructor receives values from the caller to initialize an object?

options.B: Parameterized constructor

questions.question: What is the main purpose of a copy constructor?

options.B: To create a new object from an existing object of the same class
options.D: To access private members from any function

questions.question: Which is a conventional declaration for a copy constructor of class Student?

options.B: Student(const Student& other)

questions.question: Which syntax uses a constructor initialization list?

options.B: Student(string n) : name(n) { }

questions.question: Constructor overloading means:

options.A: A class has multiple constructors with different parameter lists
options.B: A constructor has multiple return types
options.C: A constructor is inherited from every class
options.D: A constructor is converted into a namespace

questions.question: Encapsulation primarily involves:

options.A: Combining data and related operations while controlling access
options.B: Removing all methods from a class

questions.question: Information hiding refers to:

options.A: Hiding all source code from the compiler
options.B: Concealing implementation details behind a controlled interface

questions.question: Which access specifier is generally used to expose a class's public interface?

options.B: protected

questions.question: In a C++ class, members are private by default when no access specifier is written. Which keyword changes access to public?

options.B: open

questions.question: Which statement about private members is correct?

options.A: They can always be accessed directly from main()
options.B: They are directly accessible only within the class and permitted friends

questions.question: In a non-static member function, this is:

options.A: A reference to the class definition
options.B: A pointer to the current object

questions.question: Why is this->name useful in a constructor such as Student(string name)?

options.B: It distinguishes the data member name from the parameter name

questions.question: What does the new operator do in C++ when used as new Student()?

options.B: Dynamically allocates storage and constructs a Student object

questions.question: What should normally be used to release one object allocated with new?

options.B: delete

questions.question: What should be used to release an array allocated with new[]?

options.B: delete[]

questions.question: Which expression dynamically creates a Student object using a parameterized constructor?

options.B: Student s = new Student("Ali", 101);

questions.question: Which design best demonstrates encapsulation?

options.B: Private data with public methods that control access
options.C: All members declared outside the class
